title: Saily vs Airalo: prices, coverage and the small print
deck: Two travel eSIM apps whose plan tables, refund policies and activation rules are public, compared on their own published numbers — with every price dated and every vendor claim attributed.
tldr: Neither provider wins on price consistently: in the global plans the cheaper option alternates by cents, and the one clearly wide gap we found — Europe 10GB over 30 days — runs Airalo's way ($31.00 against Saily's $35.99). Saily's unlimited plan documents a higher daily full-speed allowance (5GB/day, then 1 Mbps) than Airalo's (3GB/day at 20 Mbps, then reduced speeds). Saily publishes a 30-day full-refund window for plans that were never installed or activated; Airalo processes refunds in-app and pays 'wrong purchase' cases back in app credit only.

blocks.title: How we checked this — and what we did not do
blocks.text: This comparison is based on published pricing, documentation and policies checked on October 6, 2026. Duyan did not conduct first-hand performance testing for this article. Where a statement comes from a provider describing its own product, we say so.

Saily and Airalo both publish their plan tables, refund policies and activation rules in public, and the internet is full of pages that pick a winner between them — including pages written by Saily itself and by its competitors. This page does something narrower: it puts the two providers' own published numbers side by side, dates every price, and leaves the verdict to your itinerary. Where the two companies' pages use different units or omit details, we show that instead of papering over it.

blocks.alt: A traveler holding a smartphone in an airport terminal, with luggage nearby
blocks.caption: Both apps promise the same thing: data that works the moment you land. The differences are in the plan tables and the small print.

blocks.text: The short version

**There is no consistent price winner.** Across the three destination baskets below, the cheaper provider alternates depending on the plan you pick, usually by less than a dollar. The clearer differences sit elsewhere: how each provider's unlimited plan throttles, what happens to your money when you ask for a refund, and how each counts "coverage". The rest of this page walks those differences with the dates attached.
Plans and prices, destination by destination

Each table below is a like-for-like read of the provider's own plan page on the date in its caption. Both providers sell in US dollars; neither page states at list price how taxes are handled at checkout. We compare each plan's data amount and validity exactly as listed — where the two catalogues don't offer matching shapes, we show both rows rather than force a comparison.

blocks.text: Two readings of the Japan table. On the near-matched shapes — 10GB over 30 days on both sides — Saily lists $17.99 and Airalo $18.00, which is a coin flip. At the entry level the catalogues differ for real: Saily sells a 1GB plan with 7 days of validity, while Airalo's Japan page, when we checked, listed its 1GB package under the 3-day group — we treat that as what the page showed on the check date rather than a permanent fact. Mid-size is the closest call: Airalo is cheaper on shelf price (3GB $8.00/7d, 5GB $10.00/7d, 10GB $17.00/7d), but Saily sells the same data amounts with 30-day validity at $7.99, $10.99 and $17.99.

blocks.text: Here the closest direct pairing — 10GB over 30 days — goes to Airalo: $31.00 against Saily's $35.99. But check the validity windows before choosing on price alone: Saily sells 3GB for 30 days at $12.49, while Airalo's $11.00 3GB plan covers 7 days. A two-week trip that needs 3GB pays Saily $12.49 or buys Airalo's 15-day 5GB at $19.00. And the two "Europe" plans do not cover the same map: Saily's page names a 35-country list, Airalo's page says 41 "Countries and Networks" — different labels, and neither page's list is a superset we verified. Both providers publish their country lists; check your specific stops against both before buying.

blocks.text: The global plans are the closest-matched pair in this comparison — most data amounts and validity windows line up exactly — and they are nearly identical on price: Airalo takes 1GB by 49 cents, Saily takes 2GB by a cent and 5GB by $1.01, Airalo takes 10GB by a cent and 20GB by 99 cents. Read that as parity, not a ranking. (Airalo's 3GB/30-day at $24.00 has no Saily counterpart in this table — Saily jumps from 2GB to 5GB.) On breadth, the pages' own labels differ — Saily's listing says 121 countries, Airalo's says 168 "Countries and Networks", a unit that mixes countries with network counts — so we can't tell you which plan covers more places from these labels alone. If you are heading somewhere off the main tourist lines, check that country against both providers' lists directly.
Coverage: what the numbers on the pages say

You will see four figures quoted for these two, and they are not the same unit. Saily's all-destinations page said "209 destinations found" on the check date; its global plan listing says 121 countries. Airalo's site says "200+ locations" overall, and its Discover global page says 168 "Countries and Networks" — a unit that mixes countries with network counts. Destinations and locations count entries in a store; countries do not. Per Airalo's own site, it serves "over 30 million" customers; Saily presents itself as from the makers of NordVPN (its homepage carries a "By the creators of" label with a NordVPN logo, and NordSec B.V. appears in Saily's terms as a payment provider). Both statements are the providers describing themselves. Nothing in these figures lets either provider claim a coverage win over the other, and neither company's fine print suggests otherwise.
Installation and activation, per the providers' documentation

Both providers install through an app and activate against a destination network, but their activation policies differ in a way that matters if you buy early. **Saily** states on its plan pages that all plans activate automatically when you reach your destination, or 180 days after purchase at the latest — a single rule across the catalogue. **Airalo** treats activation as a per-eSIM property: its help centre says validity starts when the eSIM activates at the destination for most eSIMs, but some activate at installation regardless of location, and the activation policy for each package is listed under "Additional Information" before purchase. If your trip is months away, Saily's uniform 180-day window is the easier rule to reason about; with Airalo, check the activation policy line on the specific package.
Hotspot and top-ups

**Hotspot:** both providers document tethering. Saily's help centre walks through personal-hotspot setup on iOS and Android with no stated restrictions. Airalo's help centre allows hotspot "as long as it is supported by your device and the network", and notes that some eSIMs require a manually-set APN for the hotspot to work — an extra step on certain packages, not a blanket ban. Per its unlimited-packages page, Airalo also states that its unlimited eSIMs come with "full hotspot support built in" (that statement is Airalo describing its own product).

**Top-ups:** Saily documents topping up any of its data plans from within the app, plus an auto top-up option. Airalo tops up only packages marked rechargeable — the help centre says to check the "Additional information" tab before purchase, and that a missing Top-up button means the eSIM is non-rechargeable and you should buy a new one. For a single defined trip this rarely matters; for an open-ended one, Saily's uniform top-up rule is simpler.
Unlimited plans: read the daily allowance first

Both providers sell "unlimited" plans, and both mean a daily full-speed allowance rather than unlimited speed forever — the details are the most important small print in this comparison. Per Saily's plan pages, its unlimited plans include 5GB per day at full speed, dropping to 1 Mbps after that. Per Airalo's unlimited-packages FAQ, its unlimited plans give 3GB per day at 20 Mbps, after which speeds are reduced, with the allowance resetting every 24 hours. Saily's documented daily allowance is larger: 5GB against Airalo's 3GB. After the cap the two are not directly comparable from the pages — Saily names a concrete 1 Mbps floor, while Airalo says only "reduced speeds" without a number, and 1 Mbps sits far below the 20 Mbps Airalo quotes for its own full-speed stage. Airalo's unlimited line starts cheaper — $11.50 for 3 days in Japan or Europe against Saily's 15-day $48.99 minimum — so for a short heavy-use weekend Airalo's unlimited can be the better buy, while a two-week work trip leans toward Saily's documented 5GB/day. These terms come from each provider's own pages; we have not tested real-world speeds.
Refunds: two different philosophies with your money

This is where the providers differ most sharply. **Saily's refund policy** promises a full refund within 30 days of purchase if the eSIM was never installed or the plan never activated. Once a plan is activated, Saily treats it as used — a further refund is considered only for Saily-side quality issues or if more than 99% of the plan remains. **Airalo** handles refunds through an in-app "Request Refund" button for eligible orders (expired or fully-used eSIMs don't qualify), and the payment route depends on the reason: 'Wrong purchase' and 'Plans changed' are refunded only in Airmoney, Airalo's in-app credit, while 'Installation issues' and 'eSIM not working' can choose Airmoney or a refund to the original payment method, which takes 7–10 business days (up to 30, per Airalo's help page). An uninstalled Airalo eSIM can also be shared to another traveler instead of refunded.

Practically: if your plan is firm and you might change your mind before travel, Saily's documented 30-day cash-back window is the clearer protection. If your plans are volatile, note that with Airalo a 'plans changed' refund arrives as app credit, not money back — that credit is only worth holding if you expect to book with Airalo again.
Privacy and extras

Saily ships extra features its parent positions as security tools: per Saily's own site and terms, these include virtual location changes, malicious-domain blocking and an ad blocker, and the app can add a US phone number for calls and texts at $1.99/month with identity verification required. Airalo's extras are travel-shaped rather than security-shaped: per its own site, the app supports 53 languages and multiple currencies, and its Discover global eSIM line includes data/calls/texts packages. We did not evaluate any security claim as a feature test — these are the providers describing their own products.
Who should choose which

items: **A one-country trip with light data needs:** compare the entry plans directly — Saily's 1GB/7-day Japan plan existed on the check date while Airalo's 1GB sat in its 3-day group; mid-size is the closest call, because Airalo's 3GB/7-day at $8.00 costs a cent more than Saily's 3GB/30-day at $7.99 and covers less than half the days. Price the exact days you need.

**A multi-country Europe trip on a data budget:** Airalo's 10GB/30-day at $31.00 beat Saily's $35.99 on the check date — but verify your countries against both providers' lists, since the two "Europe" plans cover different maps.
**Heavy data use:** Saily's documented 5GB/day full-speed allowance beats Airalo's 3GB/day at 20 Mbps for sustained use; Airalo's unlimited line starts cheaper for a short weekend of heavy streaming.
**A long multi-region trip:** the global plans are near-identical on price; decide on coverage lists and activation policy rather than the price column.
**A refund-sensitive buyer:** Saily's 30-day full-refund window for uninstalled plans is the more legible protection; with Airalo, a 'wrong purchase' refund comes back as in-app credit only.
**Trips months away:** Saily states one activation rule for all plans (arrival, or 180 days); Airalo requires checking each package's activation policy.

blocks.text: And to say it plainly: on price alone there is no consistent winner across everything we compared on October 6, 2026 — the global plans alternate by cents, and the one clearly wide gap we found, Europe 10GB over 30 days, runs Airalo's way. The decision is made by your itinerary, your data appetite and how much you value a cash refund.

items.q: Which is cheaper, Saily or Airalo?
items.a: Neither consistently. On the plan pairs we compared on October 6, 2026, the cheaper provider alternates: Airalo took Europe 10GB/30-day ($31.00 vs $35.99), the global plans differed by cents in both directions, and near-matched Japan 10GB/30-day plans were $17.99 vs $18.00. Price the specific plan for your trip instead of picking a brand on price.

items.q: Do Saily and Airalo support hotspot (tethering)?
items.a: Both document hotspot support. Saily's help centre describes standard personal-hotspot setup on iOS and Android; Airalo's says hotspot works where the device and network support it, and that some eSIMs need a manually-set APN for hotspot. Airalo also states its unlimited eSIMs include full hotspot support (its own claim).

items.q: Can I get a refund if I buy the wrong plan?
items.a: Saily: a full refund within 30 days if the eSIM was never installed or activated. After activation it treats the plan as used, with exceptions for provider-side quality issues or if over 99% of data remains. Airalo: refunds run through an in-app button for eligible orders; 'wrong purchase' and 'plans changed' are refunded in Airmoney (in-app credit) only, while installation issues and faults can be refunded to the original payment method in 7–10 business days.

items.q: Are the unlimited plans really unlimited?
items.a: They are unlimited in duration of use, not in speed. Saily documents 5GB per day at full speed, then 1 Mbps. Airalo documents 3GB per day at 20 Mbps, then reduced speeds, resetting every 24 hours. Both come from the providers' own plan terms.

Their own labels aren't comparable: Saily's site says 200+ destinations overall and 121 countries for its global plan; Airalo's says 200+ locations overall and 168 'Countries and Networks' for its Discover global eSIM. Different units, different lists. Check your specific destinations against both providers' published country lists.

items.q: Do these eSIMs come with a phone number for calls and texts?
items.a: Saily sells a US phone number add-on ($1.99/month, identity verification required, per its site). Airalo's Discover global line includes some data/calls/texts packages (per its site); the standard country and regional plans on both providers are data-only on the pages we checked.

items.q: Can I reuse the same eSIM on another trip?
items.a: Saily positions its app as one eSIM you add new destinations to. Airalo sells separate eSIMs per package and tops up only packages marked rechargeable — check the 'Additional information' tab before purchase.

items.q: When does an Airalo or Saily plan expire if I buy early?
items.a: Saily states a single rule on its plan pages: plans activate at your destination or 180 days after purchase, whichever comes first. Airalo's validity starts when the eSIM activates; most activate at the destination but some activate at installation regardless of location, and the activation policy is listed per package before you buy.
